request.spec:
On the sheet a transfer brought a person to, a steward can undo it on the same sheet-today they
arrived (a button on the row; any later day, anyone else, or a person who did not arrive by transfer
is refused with an error on the row): the person is transferred back to the sheet they came from by
exactly the transfer rules and lines, and this sheet then writes PERSON_TRANSFER_UNDONE name=<name>
to=<sheet id>.
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
On the sheet a transfer brought a person to, a steward can undo it on the same sheet-today they
arrived (a button on the row; any later day, anyone else, or a person who did not arrive by transfer
is refused with an error on the row): the person is transferred back to the sheet they came from by
exactly the transfer rules and lines, and this sheet then writes PERSON_TRANSFER_UNDONE name=<name>
to=<sheet id>.

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
I've added undo-transfer, and its acceptance test (`transfer undo`) passes. Of the other three tests in the spec, scenarios 1 and 3 pass. Scenario 2 still fails, but it fails in exactly the same place with my change removed, so I left it alone.

**What changed**
- **Stored data:** a new migration, `V86__person_arrived_on.sql`, adds an `arrived_on` date to each person. `ApplyTransfer` fills it with the receiving sheet's today when someone arrives by transfer. A person merged into someone, cloned in from another sheet, or added directly has no arrival date, so their undo is refused.
- **Server:** a new endpoint, `PUT /api/sheets/{sheetId}/people/{personId}/transfer-undo`. Its new check, `ValidateTransferUndo`, refuses anyone who isn't a steward, a person who didn't arrive by transfer, or a sheet whose today is no longer the arrival day. If the check passes, it sends the person back to the sheet they came from through the existing `ApplyTransfer` and `AuditPersonTransferred`, so the transfer rules and audit lines are exactly those of a normal transfer. A new `AuditTransferUndone` then writes `PERSON_TRANSFER_UNDONE … name=<name> to=<sheet>`, followed by this sheet's totals lines, which is what the test expects.
- **Front end:** a new row cell, `features/people/transferUndo.slot.tsx`, adds the `person-transfer-undo` button. A refusal shows `person-error` on the row.

**The scenario 2 failure:** it stops at `acceptance.spec.ts:680`. Editing an amount inline, for a claim that seems to fall due in the closed period P2, goes through when the test expects it to be refused. That's an existing rule about closed periods, not part of undoing a transfer, so I didn't change it. Scenario 3 also failed in the run without my change and in my first run with it, then passed twice, so it looks flaky.

**A slip while checking:** to run that comparison I removed my files without a backup, because the backup copy to `/tmp` failed (no permission). I then rewrote them from the exact text I had written earlier and re-ran the full suite twice with the results above.
